correctness.rationale: All primes p≠q are treated by the unit-modulus rank-rigidity identity, exact annihilator congruences over the coprime factors, and a checked four-event inclusion–exclusion. The rank-one sector is exactly two disjoint purity configurations. Explicit polynomial forms agree with the combinatorial formulas. Exact cyclotomic checkers reproduced all 3×3 minors for N=10,15,21 without floating-point tests; finite checks corroborate, but the universal proof is independent of finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Bounded comparisons of exact statements found a boundary-case p=2 rank-two classification and a repeated-prime affine-plane rank classification, but not the odd-distinct-prime rank-one/two incidence formula. Bonami–Ghobber studies support extremizers; Delvaux–Van Barel studies maximal rank-deficient blocks and Hamming numbers; Loukaki provides sufficient nonsingularity theorems under different restrictions. Known universal determinant rigidity is acknowledged as a premise, not claimed new. An unlocated stronger result could still cover the formula.
residual_risks: A specialized third-order rank-incidence table for odd semiprime orders may exist outside the inspected sources.
The formula is an elementary consequence of known 3×3 unit-modulus rigidity plus nontrivial CRT incidence counting; some published formulation of stronger general incidence machinery might imply it.
The full PDF text was accessible for TW477 but its web screenshot renderer returned 403; the accessed text supports the limited comparisons made.

value.rationale: Exact natural rank-incidence and deterministic singularity tests for all 3×3 restrictions on a two-prime cyclic Fourier matrix address complete three-frequency interpolation failure, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice. Odd-odd factorization creates a positive rank-one stratum absent from the known 2p case; the theorem quantifies both rank losses uniformly across an infinite group family. It does not require a downstream conjecture or imply a larger-minor classification.
